suite: Module 38 — Customer Web + Restaurant Dashboard + Platform Admin on the real local backend (behavioural events sent by the real pages, the session funnel with its conversions read from the payment and order domains, the aggregation, administrators' and restaurants' reports, market and location scope, finance figures against the finance module, exports through a queued job) with a queue worker and the DEVELOPMENT payment provider (PAYMENT_DRIVER=fake) — NO MONEY MOVES; the figures are those of this run's test orders, not business figures; commission plans are TEST FIXTURES; no behavioural history exists before Module 38

results.name: A0 the whole customer journey works through the real pages with the event emitter on: journey planned (201), restaurants listed, an item added (201), a pickup time chosen (200), the checkout confirmed (200), the payment started (201) and the order confirmed

A1 the pages sent the ten behavioural events of the registry to POST /analytics/events — each exactly ONCE as designed, although the list was re-sorted and the restaurant page reloaded — in batches, under one session identifier the application made up

A2 what a page sends is the contract and nothing more: {session, platform, events} with ids, names, times, references by id and the allowlisted properties — no phone number, no e-mail address, no name, no place, no coordinate, no amount

A3 what the server stored of them: the signed-in customer as a 32-character keyed hash (never the id or the phone number), the journey as a keyed hash (never its id), the checkout reference because the checkout is this customer's own, the restaurant and market resolved by the server
A4 the BACKEND recorded its own answers: the planned journey as bands (no length, no place, no route) and one impression per restaurant it returned — not doubled by the re-sort

A5 after the aggregation the session stands at stage 11 of the funnel: stages 1–8 from its own events, 9–11 read from the payment and the order of ITS checkout (verified payment, order created, order completed)

B1 THE EVENT DOOR IS UNREACHABLE for a whole purchase (every send of the emitter fails as a lost connection does — also the last send of a page being left; each batch is tried once more and then dropped): the customer adds an item, chooses a time, confirms the checkout, pays and gets the order exactly as always — nothing on any page mentions analytics, no error is shown, and no event of the application was stored (what the backend records by itself — the restaurants it returned — does not pass that door)
C1 the same event id is stored once: a batch sent again (the application never got the answer) adds only what is new — 202 both times

C2 A CLIENT CANNOT REPORT A PAYMENT OR AN ORDER: "payment_verified", "order_created", "order_completed" and "refund_completed" are not events (unknown_event), and an event only the backend records is refused too (not_a_client_event) — nothing is stored

C3 a property that is not on the list (a phone number, an amount), a value outside its rule, an event older than 72 hours and a restaurant that does not exist are each refused for that event — the registry is a closed list

C4 somebody else's checkout id proves nothing (a guest naming Rahul's checkout: unknown_reference); the request is a closed list (an extra "customer_id": 422), a session is a random id (a device identifier: 422), a batch has a size (26 events: 422), and without consent nothing is kept (202, stored false)

C5 EVENTS ALONE NEVER MAKE A PAYMENT OR AN ORDER: a session that claims every stage for a checkout nobody paid stops at stage 8 ("payment started") — no payment was verified, no order exists for it, and the payment and order tables are as they were

D1 THE FUNNEL (sessions, today): three sessions searched a journey; one of them — the real one — has a verified payment, an order and a completed order; the forged one stops at "payment started"; every conversion carries its numerator and denominator

D2 ORDERS: the report's counts and GMV are the order domain's own — orders placed, orders completed and the sum of the completed orders' totals — with the still-waiting order in neither side of the completion rate

D3 FINANCE: commission, platform revenue, restaurant earnings and gross marketplace sales of the report are, to the paisa, the finance module's own overview for the same day — read from the ledger at the moment of the request — and GMV is shown beside them and never called revenue

D4 ROUTES: one journey was planned, restaurants were returned for it and one order came from it; the answer is counts, bands and corridors — it holds no place, no coordinate, no route and no journey id, and says that none is stored

D5 THE OVERVIEW is eight defined figures and a headline of each area (not forty cards); the restaurant table has Burger Hub's two orders; every answer says its period, time zone, currency and that it is an AGGREGATED read (never "live") with the time of the last aggregation

D6 NO FIGURE WITHOUT A DEFINITION: all 118 different figures returned by the fifteen administrator reports are in the metric catalog (120 definitions, each with a source, a time zone, a currency rule and a freshness; every rate with its numerator and denominator); the counts of this moment are labelled OPERATIONAL and are not cached

E1 A RESTAURANT READS ITS OWN FIGURES ONLY: the owner of Riverside sees its orders of today; the owner of Second Kitchen sees none of them and gets 404 on every one of the seven reports when naming Burger Hub in the query string; Riverside's owner gets 404 for a Second Kitchen location; order staff (no analytics permission) get 403

E2 A MANAGER OF SOME LOCATIONS reads those and no other location of the same organization (naming one answers 404); without a location the owner's report covers every location, the manager's only theirs; no answer names a customer
E3 a restaurant's EARNINGS in analytics are the finance module's own summary, identical to the Earnings page (same per-currency figures), read from the ledger and not cached

E4 ADMINISTRATORS: a support administrator (no analytics permission) is refused (403); an onboarding administrator (analytics and support access, no finance access) reads the overview with its support figure, but its finance figures come back "restricted" — never a zero — and the finance report is refused (403) while the support report is theirs (200); nobody without an administrator's session gets in (401)

E5 THE MARKET IS THE SERVER'S DECISION: an operations administrator whose permission is for India asking for "all" markets gets India only; naming another market is refused (403) whatever the query string says; a market that does not exist is 404

F1 AN EXPORT IS BUILT IN THE BACKGROUND: asking answers 202 with status QUEUED at once; the queue worker builds the CSV; it becomes READY with a row count and an expiry about 24 hours away; the download is an attachment that no cache may keep

F2 THE FILE: a title line (report, period, time zone), a header line, one line per order of today with its number, status, restaurant and total — and no customer: no name, no phone number, no e-mail address

F5 EXPORT PERMISSIONS: reading analytics is not exporting it (onboarding administrator: 403); the financial report needs the finance export permission on top (operations administrator: 403; finance administrator: 202 and READY); there is no free query (an extra "sql" field: 422) and no report outside the curated list (422)

F8 AN EXPORT EXPIRES: past its time the download answers 410 export_expired, its status is EXPIRED with no download path, and its file is deleted from the private disk
